title: Code Mode: I built a Rust tool to cut >60% of your Agent API Costs?
author: legend-of-alan
selftext:
Hey all, so I don’t know if you saw the [Anthropic](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/11/17/anthropic-claude-code-code-mode-javascript-tool-calls/) from Anthropic, but they released this feature called ‘Code Mode’ for Claude Code. Basically it ‘batches’ LLM tool calls into scripts instead of constantly asking the LLM for the next tool. ***They claim 95% token savings*** (Haven't benchmarked it myself yet, but [independent research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19123) claim more like a 60% savings, depending on workload). Up to now, this is mostly used by established coding agent products like Claude Code and Codex.

I immediately became obsessed, because[ if you missed it](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/RFDKh98GyP), I’m making an engine for AI RPG games & private servers called Spookery. One, since AI game dev is dominated by token costs (which is why it’s so commercially ‘hard’ right now), this seemed important. Two, it looked like fun. So I took a look around, and there’s not much in Rust. There’s a few libraries like with TypeScript and other backends, but they’re like[ 5x slower (execution) to 100x slower (startup)](https://pydantic.dev/docs/monty/get-started/) compared to claims of modern options like Pydantic’s Monty (Python backend written on Rust).

So **I went temporarily insane, didn’t sleep, and built/released my own in the days I had off… I call it Ghost Mode**. It’s MIT-licensed, because I wanted to share it with others. To use it, just run:

    cargo add ghostmode

Give it a try if you’re looking to save tokens in your new Rust agents (or if you just want to flatter me by testing it). If anybody tries it and likes it, I think we can build a really powerful Code Mode implementation together (extend it for other languages, add new features, etc.).

I hope you get something useful out of it. I’ll be back soon with more Spookery updates too, now that I’m pushing a completely new `ratatui` client (instead of the janky terminal in there now).

And if you get nothing out of this, just keep an eye for code mode in your code harnesses soon. I think Anthropic’s is still in the experimental features… But I think it’ll change the game if it’s as powerful as the research says.
